title: Crossplane State Metrics
description: Per-object health and configuration drift for every Crossplane object in the cluster, plus the exporter's own golden signals.

panels.title: Objects Observed
panels.description: Every Crossplane object the exporter can see, of every kind.

panels.title: Kinds Watched
panels.description: Crossplane CRD kinds currently informed on. Discovered, never enumerated: installing a provider raises this with no config change.

panels.title: Objects Not Ready
panels.description: Objects whose Ready condition is not True. Any is worth looking at, so the threshold is one.

panels.title: Objects Not Synced
panels.description: Objects Crossplane could not reconcile. Not Synced usually precedes not Ready.

panels.title: Managed Resources Drifted
panels.description: Managed resources whose observed state no longer matches what git declares.

panels.title: Managed Resources Compared
panels.description: Managed resources drift was computed for. Compare with Objects Observed: the difference is the objects that have no forProvider to compare.

panels.title: Objects By Readiness
panels.description: Ready condition across every Crossplane kind over time.

panels.title: Drifted Managed Resources By Kind
panels.description: Drift is compared only for managed resources: they are the only kinds carrying both spec.forProvider and status.atProvider.

panels.title: Unhealthy Objects
panels.description: Every Crossplane object in a non-True condition, with the reason the controller gave. One table covers managed resources, composites, packages and definitions alike, because they all carry the same condition shape.

panels.title: Drifted Managed Resources
panels.description: Managed resources whose cloud state has diverged from the declared spec. Enable drift-fields to see which fields differ.

panels.title: Package Health
panels.description: A provider going unhealthy is why hundreds of managed resources stop syncing. This is the causal layer above the fleet panels.

panels.title: Composition Revisions
panels.description: A Composition carries no status conditions at all, so revision count is the signal it does have. A count climbing steadily is a Composition being edited under running composites.

panels.title: Packages Not Healthy
panels.description: Providers, functions and configurations that are not installed or not healthy.

panels.title: Inactive Managed Resource Definitions
panels.description: Crossplane v2 definitions that are switched off. An inactive definition means its CRD is never created, so that managed resource kind does not exist in the cluster and produces no other metric at all - this panel is the only place that absence is visible.

panels.title: Managed Resource Definitions By State
panels.description: Crossplane v2 no longer installs every CRD a provider knows how to manage. Definitions arrive Inactive and are activated deliberately, so this is the count of kinds that exist versus kinds that are available but switched off.

panels.title: Definitions Not Established
panels.description: Composite resource definitions the API server has not accepted. Nothing downstream of an unestablished XRD can work.

panels.title: Scrape Rate
panels.description: Traffic: how often Prometheus is collecting.

panels.title: Error Rate
panels.description: Errors by source. Informer sync errors are also how a missing RBAC grant announces itself: the kind is discovered, the watch is denied, and it shows up here.

panels.title: Scrape Duration
panels.description: Latency: time to walk every informer cache and build the metric set. This is an SLO budget, not a resource ratio, so the thresholds are absolute — and they are set against the ServiceMonitor's 50s scrape timeout.

panels.title: Saturation
panels.description: Scrapes overlapping, and informers still completing their initial list. Either being persistently above zero means metrics are incomplete or collection cannot keep up.

panels.title: Series Emitted vs Cap
panels.description: Series the state collector produced last scrape. Size this against --max-series before you reach it: at four series per managed resource, a growing Crossplane estate walks straight into the cap.

panels.title: Scrape Truncated
panels.description: 1 means the series cap was reached and the scrape was cut short, so the metrics are incomplete. Truncation is deterministic, but which objects survive is arbitrary. Alert on this.

panels.title: Aggregated Kinds
panels.description: Kinds reported as counts instead of per object, because they exceeded --aggregate-threshold. Per-object drilldown for these is deliberately absent.

panels.title: Drift Computation Time
panels.description: Time spent comparing every managed resource in one scrape. Results are memoised by resourceVersion, so a steady fleet costs almost nothing and a spike means real churn.

panels.title: Kubernetes API Request Rate
panels.description: Every outbound call to the API server, by response code. 403s here mean an API group is missing from the ClusterRole.

panels.title: Kubernetes API Latency
panels.description: Outbound API latency by verb, 95th percentile.

panels.title: CPU Utilization (% Of Limit)
panels.description: Are we UNDER-provisioned? Approaching the limit means CFS throttling. The query is a ratio and the threshold a constant percent, so both survive a resource resize.

panels.title: CPU Utilization (% Of Request)
panels.description: Are we OVER-provisioned? Riding far below 100% means reserved capacity nobody uses, which wastes node allocatable and hurts bin-packing — lower the request. Riding above 100% means under-requested and at risk of eviction under node pressure — raise it.

panels.title: CPU Throttling (% Of Periods)
panels.description: The leading indicator. A CPU-limited exporter throttles before its scrape latency visibly climbs, so this moves first.

panels.title: Memory Utilization (% Of Limit)
panels.description: Approaching the memory limit means an OOM kill, not a slowdown. The informer caches hold every watched object, so this scales with fleet size.

panels.title: Memory Utilization (% Of Request)
panels.description: Usage against the reservation. Persistently far below 100% is capacity nobody uses; persistently above is an under-requested pod in Burstable QoS.

panels.title: Memory Working Set
panels.description: Absolute memory, for sizing the requests and limits the panels above are measured against.

panels.title: Exporter Logs
panels.description: Structured JSON logs. Records emitted inside a span carry trace_id and span_id, so a log line links straight to its trace.

panels.title: Recent Traces
panels.description: Spans emitted by the exporter. Tracing is a no-op unless OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT is set, so this panel is empty until a collector is configured.
